examples.text: А мне это шоу завтра вести!
examples.trans: And I have to host that show tomorrow!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'about' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Помнишь, я рассказывал про свои сны?
examples.trans: Do you remember I told you about my dreams?

examples.text: Подожди, ты про Вику во сне?
examples.trans: Wait, you mean Vika in your dream?

examples.text: Я просто рассказывал Косте про сны.
examples.trans: I was just telling Kostya about my dreams.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'video recording', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: А про нашу видеозапись ты забыл?
examples.trans: And did you forget about our video recording?

examples.text: Смотри на видеозапись камеры.
examples.trans: Look at the camera's video recording.

examples.text: Видеозапись сохранена на диске.
examples.trans: The video recording is saved on the drive.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'быть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to forget', forming an aspectual pair with 'забывать'.

examples.text: Извините, я просто забыл отключить.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I just forgot to turn it off.

examples.text: А голову ты дома не забыл?
examples.trans: And did you not forget your head at home?

examples.text: А про нашу видеозапись ты забыл?
examples.trans: And did you forget about our video recording?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('really') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы разве ещё совсем не знаете?
examples.trans: Do you really not know at all yet?

examples.text: Разве ты не знал об этом?
examples.trans: Didn't you know about this?

examples.text: Разве это не правда?
examples.trans: Isn't that the truth?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.

examples.text: Что? Что ещё за глупый бред?
examples.trans: What? What kind of foolish nonsense is that?

examples.text: Мне ещё завтра в шоу выступать.
examples.trans: I still have to perform on the show tomorrow.

examples.text: Вы разве ещё совсем не знаете?
examples.trans: Do you really not know at all yet?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Он совсем один.
examples.trans: He's completely alone.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Не знаю, почему он так пахнет.
examples.trans: I do not know why it smells like that.

examples.text: Я не знаю, спит дома, наверное.
examples.trans: I do not know, he is probably sleeping at home.

examples.text: Подожди, об этом уже все знают?
examples.trans: Wait, does everyone know about this already?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to buy', forming an aspectual pair with 'покупать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я купил эту запись у поваров.
examples.trans: I bought that recording from your cooks.

examples.text: Я купил герметик.
examples.trans: I've bought sealant.

examples.text: Купи хлеб, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Buy some bread, please.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('this') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Так вот, этой женщиной была Вика.
examples.trans: Well then, that woman was Vika.

examples.text: Какой идиот распустил этот глупый слух?
examples.trans: What idiot spread this stupid rumor?

examples.text: Ты сам эту кашу заварил.
examples.trans: You stirred up this mess yourself.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'recording', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты сможешь показать Кате эту запись.
examples.trans: You will be able to show Katya that recording.

examples.text: Это запись из кабинета нашей Вики.
examples.trans: This is a recording from our Vika's office.

examples.text: Я купил эту запись у поваров.
examples.trans: I bought that recording from your cooks.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Дима, а где наш повар Баринов?
examples.trans: Dima, and where is our cook Barinov?

examples.text: Я купил эту запись у поваров.
examples.trans: I bought that recording from your cooks.

examples.text: Даже самым обычным рядовым поваром.
examples.trans: Not even as the most ordinary line cook.
